messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: PrivateLink endpoint pl-acme-prod in ap-southeast-1 exhibiting route instability and DNS resolution failures. Severity: P1. Affected customer: AcmeCo. Pager triggered to oncall.

Raj Patel: ACK — oncall. Jumping in. Any quick customer-facing note to send? :eyes:

Customer Success: We already have a banner up for a subset of API calls, some customers report connectivity errors. AcmeCo reached out via support ticket.

Elena Kim: Looking at DNS graphs — spike in NXDOMAIN and SERVFAIL toward pl-acme-prod resolvers starting ~3417654200. /svc/dns shows increased retries. Could be asymmetric path.

Tom Nguyen: Running quick dig from our resolver host in az-a & az-b:
```
# az-a
dig +short pl-acme-prod.internal.acme.local @10.10.10.11 -> 10.2.3.8
# az-b
dig +short pl-acme-prod.internal.acme.local @10.10.20.11 -> (sometimes empty)
```
Intermittent returns from az-b.

Sophia Chen: traceroute from az-b-edge -> pl-acme endpoint shows packet loss after transit-edge-azb-02.
```
traceroute to 10.2.3.8 (10.2.3.8), 30 hops max
 1  10.10.20.1  0.5 ms
 2  transit-edge-azb-02  1.2 ms  !H
 3  ... * * *
```

Raj Patel: Gotcha. Could be forwarding engine or NIC flapping on that transit edge device. @network-infra-bot, can you validate BFD/BGP sessions for transit-edge-azb-02? Any errors in route-reflector logs?

network-infra-bot: BGP session to transit-edge-azb-02 shows frequent TCP resets since 3417654187. BFD sessions oscillating. Adj-Routing: flaps seen for prefixes owned by pl-acme-prod. Suspect hardware NIC/firmware or vendor queueing anomaly.

Elena Kim: Customer impact: ~30% of PrivateLink traffic from az-b is failing DNS lookups and TCP connections, fallback to az-a works. Latency impact for successful flows +40% p95.

Tom Nguyen: Quick mitigation suggestion: shift PrivateLink endpoint routing for az-b subnets to prefer AZ-a path (increase local-pref / replace-route) to avoid the faulty transit node. Canary to 5% first.

Raj Patel: Agreed. Steps:
1) Create canary route change for one customer subnet to route via az-a transit.
2) Monitor DNS success-rate and connection errors for 15m.
3) If stable, progressively move other subnets.

Sophia Chen: Preparing the route update. Command I'll run (canary):
```
aws ec2 replace-route --route-table-id rtb-0abc1234 --destination-cidr-block 10.2.3.0/24 --network-interface-id eni-0a1b2c3d --region ap-southeast-1
```

Tom Nguyen: Also enabling temporary route dampening on route-reflector for prefixes from transit-edge-azb-02 to avoid oscillation propagation.

Raj Patel: Doing canary now. @Customer Success pls send a brief update to AcmeCo: we're rerouting traffic to a healthy AZ to restore connectivity; no config needed on their side. ETA 10-15m.

Customer Success: Sent. Customer acknowledged, asked for updates.

Sophia Chen: Canary applied to rtb-0abc1234. Monitoring metrics.

Elena Kim: DNS success-rate for the canary subnet rose from 68% -> 99% within 90s. Connection errors dropped to baseline. CPU on origin not impacted.

Raj Patel: Good. Proceeding to roll remaining az-b subnets in 2-minute batches. Tom, keep dampening for another 30m.

Tom Nguyen: Will do. Also opening ticket with vendor for transit-edge-azb-02 hardware, raising severity and asking for immediate firmware check.

network-infra-bot: Vendor ticket created: VEND-48721. Vendor confirmed NIC firmware/queueing regression in release 4.7.2, recommended immediate patch. ETA vendor on-site: 3 hours.

Sophia Chen: Rolling remainder of routes now. 4 more route tables updated, propagation complete. Monitoring.

Elena Kim: Aggregate DNS errors across ap-southeast-1 dropped to baseline. Customer requests re-test from their side.

Customer Success: AcmeCo confirms connectivity restored for their API traffic. They reported a visible reduction in failed requests.

Raj Patel: Marking incident as mitigated. Next steps: vendor patch scheduling, permanent route-policy to avoid single transit dependency for PrivateLink endpoints (multi-path), and postmortem. Posting short incident note to #incidents.

Tom Nguyen: Adding temporary firewall rule to block broken NIC path at edge to prevent future partial traffic acceptance while patch pending.

network-infra-bot: Firewall rule applied on transit-edge-azb-02 to blackhole problematic egress. This will keep traffic on alternate stable path.

Sophia Chen: Confirming no customer-visible degradations for 10 minutes after change. Metrics steady.

Raj Patel: Root cause (initial): transit-edge-azb-02 exhibited NIC/firmware regression causing TCP resets and route flap propagation. Impact: intermittent DNS resolution and connection failures for PrivateLink endpoints originating in az-b. Customer impact window ~35 minutes, partial for some subnets. Fix: route steering + temporary blackhole + vendor patch to follow.

Elena Kim: Postmortem owners: Raj Patel, Tom Nguyen, Sophia Chen, with network-infra. Creating INC-1234 and assigning. Action items:
- vendor patch verification (network-infra)
- implement multi-path route policy for PrivateLink (SRE/infra)
- add extra DNS resolver health checks and automated shift (platform)

Raj Patel: Handoff: Elena taking next on-call window monitoring 08:00-16:00. I'll remain reachable for postmortem.

Customer Success: Sent final update to AcmeCo with apology and brief explanation. Customer satisfied with mitigation and asks for timeline for permanent fix.

Raj Patel: Closing thread. Will link to postmortem when created. :white_check_mark:
